🔁 Ethics & Safety

Filter bubble

In simple words

When recommendation algorithms keep showing you more of what you already like or believe, so you rarely see anything else.

When the algorithms of apps and sites keep showing you things like the ones you already clicked, liked or agreed with, so different views and topics slowly disappear from your feed. The name was made popular by Eli Pariser in 2011. Researchers still argue about how strong the effect really is.

Example. Watch a few videos about one football club and soon your feed is full of that club. You can step out of the bubble on purpose: search for other views, follow different people or clear your watch history.

  • Lesson 5: AI in Everyday Life
  • Lesson 14: How Apps Choose for You

Related words

  • Recommendation systemAn AI system that suggests things you might like, based on what you and similar people chose before.
  • AlgorithmA clear, step-by-step set of instructions for solving a problem.
  • Collaborative filteringRecommending things that people with tastes like yours enjoyed, without knowing what the things are about.
